hypothesis: Expanding each tool's indexed text with N LLM-predicted user queries (Doc2Query) shifts tool embeddings closer to the query distribution, lifting recall without changing tree shape or traversal.

papers.title: Document Expansion by Query Prediction (Doc2Query)
papers.key_claim: Predicting and appending likely queries to each document achieves state-of-the-art on two retrieval benchmarks.

papers.title: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels (HyDE)
papers.key_claim: Symmetric query-side trick: LLM hallucinates a hypothetical answer document, embed that instead of the raw query; outperforms Contriever zero-shot.

design.stage: between Stage 2 (enrich) and Stage 3 (cluster_leaves) — augments the text fed into embedding
design.expansion: For each tool, prompt labeler_llm for N=5 realistic user queries; concat to enrichment.intent before embedding.
design.cache: Reuse DiskCache so re-runs are free.
files_to_touch: src/tool_index/pipeline/stage2_enrich.py (append expanded queries to text-to-embed field)
design.alternative_hyde: If Doc2Query under-delivers, try HyDE on the query side: embed an LLM-generated hypothetical tool description for each user query before traversal. Lower indexing cost, higher per-query latency.

measurement.metric: recall@10 on the 180-query synthetic eval set
measurement.command: Re-run stages 2,3,4,5 with expansion on; uv run scripts/stage_validate.py --run raw-tools
ablation: HyDE on query side, no doc expansion
measurement.success_threshold: recall@10 >= 0.94, with structural error count unchanged from v7 (3)

risks: LLM cost: N expansions per tool; mitigated by cache and small catalog (~90 tools).
Over-expansion can blur a tool's centroid into neighbors — tune N down if discriminability warnings increase.
decision_rule: Promote if recall >= 0.94 AND low-discriminability pair count does not grow vs v7. Cheapest direction to try first.
